key_insight: A physics-constrained, multi-fidelity turbulence model can make Reynolds-number growth effectively logarithmic in cost while preserving accuracy across higher-Reynolds-number flows.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical path to cheaper CFD predictions for wall-bounded turbulent flows by learning low-cost corrections that extrapolate to more demanding operating conditions.
method: Augment the Spalart–Allmaras RANS model with field inversion and machine learning.
Enforce a constrained formulation that preserves the law of the wall.
Train at affordable low-Re data and deploy to higher-Re cases under a fixed-grid, steady-solver cost model.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports successful transfer from training at Reτ=1000 to Reτ=5200 in channel flow and from Reb=5600 to Reb=10595, 19000, and 37000 in periodic hill flow, with the constrained model achieving the lowest RMSE and near Reynolds-number-independent error.
watch_item: The formal O(log(Re)) scaling depends on specific assumptions about grid alignment, fixed spanwise resolution, and steady-solver cost, so real-world performance may differ when those conditions are violated.
paper_title: A formal log(Re)-cost framework for the engineering turbulence problem
